tasks.title: Implement guarded migration apply and recovery
tasks.goal: Apply a validated migration with retained before-state, exact CAS and truthful interrupted-state recovery.
steps: Implement explicit apply for .C plans: verify input/target epoch and exact source digest, retain before-images, then publish through existing safe filesystem/journal primitives.
Support a real recognized legacy authored-format transition without guessing new source classification/feature intent; validate the resulting reader-visible format.
Inject interruption before/after each write and provide inspect/recover/idempotent replay; record completed/pending/unknown effects instead of assuming Err means no write.
positive_cases: A known legacy document migrates preserving comments, values and selected intent.
Repeated exact apply is idempotent; supported interrupted recovery restores/completes the owned prefix.
negative_cases: Concurrent source change, unknown third state or ambiguous input refuses.
A failed migration cannot silently lose source, rewrite fixtures/upstreams or fabricate successful rollback.
acceptance: Runnable fixtures cover real before→after reader behavior, preservation and recovery.
Generated report/errors retain exact source/target/effect state across process exit.
tasks.safe_stop: Migration apply/recovery foundation passes; source/feature converters remain their own atoms.
tasks.commit_subject: feat(migrate): apply exact format transitions with recovery
notes: Do not make this early foundation depend on completed M-16 editing services. Preserve an explicit adapter seam; M-16 later adds participating-buffer barriers to these same domain operations.

Schema changes: inspect the existing codegen entrypoint before regeneration; never hand-edit generated types or invent a new codegen command. The listed check-codegen and wire-diff commands are existing self-check gates.
Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.

tasks.title: Reconcile active own 1.0.0 metadata within the accepted census
tasks.goal: Apply only the exact active-owned manifest/constraint changes identified by M-13-A.
steps: Require the root-approved exact per-file M-13-A active-owned edit list before touching any nested manifest; narrow this subtree envelope to that list in the execution packet.

Update only active own product/package versions and own constraints/docs that the census proves must be 1.0.0; preserve foreign dependencies, upstream pins, historical slots/receipts, fixtures and machine epochs.

Run the preservation/version fixtures and current workspace metadata checks; report no-op items honestly and regenerate derived state only after the owning authored source is committed under root control.
positive_cases: All in-scope active own products/packages are 1.0.0 and their owned constraints agree.
negative_cases: A broad numeric replacement or editing a frozen historical slot is forbidden.
Unknown ownership or a file absent from the accepted edit list stops that edit without reopening the owner policy.
acceptance: Per-file before/after census proves exactly which active-owned items changed.
Foreign/history/fixture/epoch exclusion checks show no collateral version edits.
tasks.safe_stop: Active-own metadata reconciliation is complete within the accepted exact list.
tasks.commit_subject: chore(version): reconcile active owned metadata at 1.0.0
notes: The listed crates/ and vibepacks/ are outer closed envelopes only: execution MUST receive the exact accepted manifest/constraint file list from M-13-A; never use the subtree as permission for arbitrary edits.
This is the only intentionally inventory-derived file perimeter in this authoring slice; root must bind/narrow it before dispatch. No automatic Redbook bump, release or graduation.

Dispatch binding is mandatory: attach the accepted per-file active-owned census from M-13-A; neither broad subtree is an executable write grant. If no such binding exists, the task is not dispatch-ready.
Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.
